name: Human Origins & Ancient Worlds
description: Evidence-led episodes about the hominin record - the specimen, the site, the date and the dispute - built from named fossils, excavations, dating runs and collections, with the analytical method that turns each object into a claim about the human past.

exclusions: Do not present a contested date, affinity or attribution as settled.
Do not build the episode on prehistoric life as lived experience; the subject is the specimen, the site and the record.
Do not narrate a reconstruction of behaviour as if it were an observation.
Do not attribute a tool, a burial or an ornament to a maker the excavated record does not identify.
prompt_context: Build the episode on one bounded object and the record that carries it: a fossil, a cast, a section face, an excavation grid square, a dating run, a monograph plate, a field notebook. Name the site or stratigraphic setting and the interval, explain the biological, taphonomic, behavioural or analytical process, and say plainly how the claim is known. The subject is the hominin evidence record, not prehistoric life as lived experience. Keep observation, inference, debate and speculation separate. Where a date, an affinity or an attribution is contested, present the competing records rather than picking a winner.
compatibility_rules: Use only with the Deep Time Documentary Formula.
Keep the object, its site and interval, the mechanism, and the evidence method in every assignment.

tuples.episode_object: the CCH1 metatarsal from a Luzon cave floor
tuples.time_place_scope: Callao Cave, northern Luzon, Philippines, about 67 ka
tuples.mechanism: island populations can develop small body size over many generations of isolation

tuples.episode_object: the Deep Skull recovered from a Borneo cave mouth

tuples.episode_object: teeth taken from beneath a sealing flowstone in Hunan
tuples.time_place_scope: Fuyan Cave at Daoxian, Hunan, China, late Pleistocene

tuples.episode_object: a mandible fragment with a projecting chin from Guangxi

tuples.episode_object: teeth from a Javanese fissure fill in a museum tray

tuples.episode_object: a single-grain optical dating disc of quartz grains
tuples.time_place_scope: phase 2 of the Madjedbebe deposit, western Arnhem Land, Northern Territory
tuples.mechanism: each quartz grain stores a charge that builds after burial and empties on exposure to light

tuples.episode_object: an edge-ground hatchet head fragment

tuples.episode_object: a grinding stone with a shallow use basin
tuples.time_place_scope: the sand deposits below the shelter wall at Madjedbebe, Arnhem Land

tuples.episode_object: a sheet of reflective mica from the excavation

tuples.episode_object: a ground ochre crayon with striated facets

tuples.episode_object: a silcrete flake with a retouched edge
tuples.time_place_scope: phase 3 of the Madjedbebe sand sequence, western Arnhem Land
tuples.mechanism: silcrete carried from distant outcrops was reduced and resharpened inside the shelter
tuples.evidence_lens: raw material distances mapped from geological survey of the surrounding region

tuples.episode_object: a thumbnail scraper from the upper sands
tuples.time_place_scope: phase 5 deposits at the Madjedbebe rockshelter, Holocene occupation
tuples.mechanism: small flakes were retouched into steep-edged tools suited to working wood and hide

tuples.episode_object: a stratigraphic section drawing of squares B4 and C4

tuples.mechanism: the deposit is a sand body whose colour and compaction change gradually with depth

tuples.episode_object: the base of the sand sheet resting on bedrock
tuples.time_place_scope: the sterile sand at the foot of the Madjedbebe shelter, below the artefact layers

tuples.episode_object: a termite gallery traced through the deposit
tuples.time_place_scope: the sand body at Madjedbebe, western Arnhem Land, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: termites tunnel through sandy sediment and shift small objects vertically as they work
tuples.evidence_lens: vertical movement of artefacts tested against overdispersion in the grain age data

tuples.episode_object: a hearth of charcoal and heat-fractured stone
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper occupation phases of the Madjedbebe sand deposit
tuples.mechanism: fires set on sand fracture the stones ringing them and stain the sediment beneath

tuples.episode_object: a ground-edge axe with a hafting groove
tuples.time_place_scope: the Holocene layers at the Madjedbebe rockshelter, Northern Territory
tuples.mechanism: a groove was pecked round the body of the axe so a handle could be lashed to it

tuples.episode_object: the Kombolgie sandstone forming the shelter wall
tuples.time_place_scope: the Palaeoproterozoic sandstone escarpment of western Arnhem Land
tuples.mechanism: sandstone weathers back along joints to leave overhangs deep enough to shelter under

tuples.episode_object: the artefact plot for the lowest dense assemblage
tuples.time_place_scope: the densest artefact concentration within the lower Madjedbebe sands
tuples.mechanism: thousands of flakes accumulated in a restricted area during repeated visits to the shelter
tuples.evidence_lens: vertical spread of artefacts modelled against luminescence ages for each spit

tuples.episode_object: the ochre-covered sandstone slab from the deposit
tuples.time_place_scope: the pigment-rich horizon of the Madjedbebe sand sequence
tuples.mechanism: pigment transferred onto a flat slab used as a working surface for grinding haematite
tuples.evidence_lens: pigment on the slab matched to crayons recovered from the same excavated layers

tuples.episode_object: a dose rate probe placed in the section face
tuples.time_place_scope: the sediment profile of the Madjedbebe deposit, Northern Territory
tuples.mechanism: radioactive elements in the sand deliver a steady dose to the buried quartz grains
tuples.evidence_lens: in-situ dose rates checked against laboratory measurements on the same sediment

tuples.episode_object: the 1989 excavation records from the earlier dig
tuples.time_place_scope: the first excavation at the shelter, then recorded under its former name
tuples.mechanism: an earlier trench sampled the same sand body and found artefacts at comparable depths
tuples.evidence_lens: earlier thermoluminescence results read against the later single-grain optical ages

tuples.episode_object: a refitted pair of flakes from adjacent spits
tuples.time_place_scope: the phase 2 artefact assemblage at the Arnhem Land shelter
tuples.mechanism: two pieces struck from one core came to rest at slightly different depths in the sand
tuples.evidence_lens: refit distances used to gauge how far pieces moved after they were dropped

tuples.episode_object: a seed grinding slab with adhering starch residue
tuples.time_place_scope: the plant processing evidence in the lower Madjedbebe layers
tuples.mechanism: seeds crushed against a stone surface leave starch granules lodged in its surface pits
tuples.evidence_lens: starch granules identified against a reference collection of Australian plant species

tuples.episode_object: the excavation agreement held by the Mirarr traditional owners
tuples.time_place_scope: the Madjedbebe site on Mirarr land in the Jabiluka area, Northern Territory
tuples.mechanism: the excavation ran under an agreement giving the traditional owners control of the work
tuples.evidence_lens: the agreement's terms recorded alongside the published account of both field seasons

coverage_profiles.subject: the Mungo burials of the Willandra Lakes

tuples.episode_object: the cremated and crushed remains catalogued as Lake Mungo 1
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mungo Unit of the Lake Mungo lunette, about 50 to 40 ka

tuples.episode_object: the quartz grains extracted from the sand around the graves

tuples.mechanism: quartz buried in a dune absorbed a radiation dose after its last exposure to daylight

tuples.episode_object: the freshwater mussel shell middens along the old shoreline

tuples.episode_object: the quartz sand beds forming the lowest dune unit

tuples.episode_object: the gypsum-rich sediment capping the dune sequence

tuples.episode_object: the hearth stones and fire-reddened sediment on a bare surface
tuples.time_place_scope: the deflation hollows on the Mungo lunette surface, Holocene
tuples.mechanism: wind stripped the loose sand and left harder fire-affected material standing proud
tuples.evidence_lens: hearth positions surveyed and dated to tie surface features to buried stratigraphy

tuples.episode_object: the human footprint impressions preserved in a hardened clay pan
tuples.time_place_scope: the fossil trackway surface in the Willandra lakes, about 20 ka
tuples.mechanism: feet pressed into wet clay that dried and hardened before being covered by sand
tuples.evidence_lens: the trackways recorded photogrammetrically and read for stride, stature and direction

tuples.episode_object: the channel sands traced across the dry lake floor
tuples.time_place_scope: the Willandra distributary channel of the Lachlan system, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: an overflow channel from an inland river fed the lake chain when the catchment was wet

tuples.episode_object: the emu eggshell fragments recovered from the dune sand
tuples.time_place_scope: the Willandra Lakes Region in southwestern New South Wales, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: eggs were collected and cooked, and shell fragments entered the surrounding sediment
tuples.evidence_lens: amino acid racemisation on that eggshell compared with the sediment luminescence results

tuples.episode_object: the stone artefact scatters mapped on a northern lake's lunette
tuples.time_place_scope: Lake Garnpung on the northern lakes, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: silcrete and quartz were flaked at lakeside camps and left as surface scatters
tuples.evidence_lens: those scatters compared with the Mungo lunette material for raw material and reduction

tuples.episode_object: the fish otoliths and golden perch bones from a shore deposit
tuples.time_place_scope: Lake Leaghur in the Willandra system, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: fish taken from a full freshwater lake were cooked and their bones left on the shore
tuples.evidence_lens: otolith growth rings read for the season in which the fish were caught

tuples.episode_object: the lunette section logged on a lake further up the chain
tuples.time_place_scope: Lake Mulurulu in the same lake chain, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: each lake in the chain built its own crescent dune on its downwind shore
tuples.evidence_lens: sections correlated between lakes by unit description and by luminescence ages

tuples.episode_object: the catchment gauge records of modern river flow
tuples.time_place_scope: the Lachlan River catchment feeding the lake chain, Quaternary
tuples.mechanism: highland runoff fed the western river system that once filled the now-dry lake basins
tuples.evidence_lens: modern flow records used to model the discharge needed to fill the lake chain

tuples.episode_object: the cave floor deposits with stone tools and hearth material
tuples.time_place_scope: Devil's Lair in southwestern Australia, about 48 ka
tuples.mechanism: a limestone cave accumulated occupation debris in a well-stratified sequence
tuples.evidence_lens: the Devil's Lair radiocarbon series compared with the Willandra luminescence chronology

tuples.episode_object: the ground-edge hatchet fragments from the shelter's lowest layers
tuples.time_place_scope: Madjedbebe rockshelter in northern Australia, about 65 ka
tuples.mechanism: artefacts accumulated in sandy shelter deposits at the base of a sandstone escarpment
tuples.evidence_lens: the Madjedbebe optical ages argued against the taphonomic mixing objections raised there

tuples.episode_object: WLH 50, a thick-boned calvaria collected from bare ground

tuples.mechanism: a heavy skull was exposed by deflation and collected without a stratigraphic context
tuples.evidence_lens: its vault thickness compared with the other Willandra remains and regional samples

tuples.episode_object: the register recording the return of ancestral remains to country
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mungo National Park keeping place, since 2017

tuples.evidence_lens: that register cross-read with the original excavation catalogues to account for each individual

tuples.episode_object: the numbered survey pegs set across the eroding dune
tuples.time_place_scope: the field survey grids on the Mungo lunette, the 1969 to 1974 seasons
tuples.mechanism: an eroding dune was walked in transects so surface finds were recorded to fixed positions
tuples.evidence_lens: survey records compared with later resurveys to measure how fast the scarp retreats

coverage_profiles.subject: the footprint surfaces of the Tularosa Basin

tuples.episode_object: a human footprint preserved as a filled impression

tuples.mechanism: a foot pressed into saturated marl and the deformed sediment was buried by the next layer

tuples.episode_object: a trackway of consecutive prints crossing the flat

tuples.episode_object: a trench face cut across the buried surface

tuples.episode_object: a vial of Ruppia cirrhosa seeds from the print layer

tuples.episode_object: a quartz sand sample collected under light-proof cover

tuples.mechanism: quartz grains store a radiation signal that sunlight resets before burial

tuples.episode_object: a ground-penetrating radar profile over the trackway

tuples.episode_object: a sediment core through the palaeolake sequence

tuples.episode_object: a photogrammetric model of a single impression
tuples.time_place_scope: the exposed track surface on the northern flat, late Pleistocene

tuples.evidence_lens: the digital model compared with impressions made in experimental substrates

tuples.episode_object: a mud-cracked bedding plane above the prints

tuples.episode_object: a ghost track visible only at certain moisture levels

tuples.episode_object: an excavated block of laminated mud containing a print

tuples.episode_object: a large mammal trackway crossing the same bedding plane

tuples.episode_object: a gypsum crust sample from the playa surface

tuples.episode_object: the archived sample bags from the first dating campaign

tuples.episode_object: a section drawing of the print-bearing beds

tuples.episode_object: an ostracod-bearing marl sample from the sequence

tuples.mechanism: ostracods lived in shallow saline water and their shells settled into the marl

tuples.episode_object: a shoreline gravel ridge mapped around the basin

tuples.episode_object: a set of small prints among the larger ones

tuples.mechanism: feet of different sizes pressed into the same soft layer over a short span of time

tuples.episode_object: a graphite target pressed for accelerator dating

tuples.episode_object: a human hair strand recovered from the sediment

tuples.episode_object: a stemmed biface base from the cave floor

tuples.episode_object: a sagebrush twig dated beside the faecal material

tuples.evidence_lens: twig ages compared with the ages obtained on the faecal specimens

tuples.episode_object: a page from the 1938 field notebook

tuples.evidence_lens: the notebook record compared with the later stratigraphic sections

tuples.episode_object: a camel metapodial from the cave deposits

tuples.evidence_lens: the faunal list compared with other Great Basin cave sequences

tuples.episode_object: a volcanic ash sample taken from the section

tuples.episode_object: a profile sketch of the Cave 5 western wall

tuples.episode_object: a screen residue tray of seeds and fibre

tuples.episode_object: a sediment column sampled for soluble salts

tuples.episode_object: the conservation record for the older cave collections

tuples.evidence_lens: the treatment record checked against the pretreatment used before dating

tuples.episode_object: an obsidian flake sourced by X-ray fluorescence
tuples.time_place_scope: the artefact-bearing beds of the cave cluster, Oregon, terminal Pleistocene

tuples.episode_object: a grid square record from the 2003 season

tuples.evidence_lens: the square records compared with the total station plotting of the same finds

tuples.evidence_lens: crown outlines compared with the Denisova molars and with the Xujiayao dental sample

tuples.episode_object: the Xiahe 2 rib fragment found in the excavation
tuples.time_place_scope: layer 3 of the excavated cave fill, Xiahe County, Gansu, about 48 to 32 ka
tuples.mechanism: a rib splinter lay among butchered animal bone in a layer of ordinary occupation debris
tuples.evidence_lens: collagen fingerprinting picked the human fragment out of thousands of animal bones

tuples.episode_object: the sediment samples extracted for ancient DNA
tuples.time_place_scope: the dated fill of the cave, Ganjia Basin, Gansu, about 100 ka
tuples.mechanism: DNA shed from bodies binds to sediment particles and survives in cold dry cave deposits
tuples.evidence_lens: mitochondrial reads from the sediment tied to the layers dated by luminescence

tuples.episode_object: the quartz aliquots measured for optical dating
tuples.time_place_scope: the sampled column through the cave deposits, Gansu, about 60 ka
tuples.mechanism: buried quartz stores a signal that grows with the radiation dose from surrounding sediment
tuples.evidence_lens: the age model built layer by layer to place each genetic and faunal result

tuples.episode_object: the cut-marked blue sheep bones from the fill
tuples.time_place_scope: the faunal assemblage of the cave, Tibetan Plateau margin, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: Pseudois nayaur carcasses were carried in, filleted and broken open for their marrow
tuples.evidence_lens: cut and percussion marks counted against the carnivore damage on the same bones

tuples.episode_object: the woolly rhinoceros bone from the lower layers
tuples.time_place_scope: the cold stage deposits inside the cave, Gansu, about 120 ka
tuples.mechanism: cold-adapted large mammals ranged onto the plateau edge during colder intervals
tuples.evidence_lens: the species list read against the Chinese loess record of glacial and interglacial cycles

tuples.episode_object: the simple flake tools recovered during excavation
tuples.time_place_scope: the artefact-bearing levels of the cave, Xiahe County, Gansu, Palaeolithic fill
tuples.mechanism: local stone was flaked with direct percussion into scrapers and unretouched cutting flakes
tuples.evidence_lens: the industry compared with the northern Chinese core and flake assemblages

tuples.episode_object: the excavation grid opened inside the cave in 2018
tuples.time_place_scope: the cave floor at the Ganjia Basin site, Gansu, Pleistocene fill
tuples.mechanism: controlled squares replaced an accidental find with a recorded stratified sequence
tuples.evidence_lens: the grid record used to place the earlier chance find within a known deposit

tuples.episode_object: the section face cut through the cave sediments
tuples.time_place_scope: the stratified deposit at the cave entrance, Ganjia Basin, about 190 ka
tuples.mechanism: silt washed in from the plateau surface interleaved with roof debris to fill the cavity
tuples.evidence_lens: the section correlated with the dating samples taken from each described unit

tuples.episode_object: the surface scan file of the jaw and its crust
tuples.time_place_scope: the specimen curated at Lanzhou, Gansu, from a middle Pleistocene context
tuples.mechanism: a digital surface model records shape without further damage to a heavily coated fossil
tuples.evidence_lens: the scan used for the virtual removal of the crust before shape comparison

tuples.episode_object: the reconstructed dental arcade from the scan
tuples.time_place_scope: the Tibetan Plateau above three thousand metres, western China, Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: mirroring one preserved half restores the full width of a jaw broken at the midline
tuples.evidence_lens: the mirrored arcade measured against the Chinese archaic hominin mandibular series

tuples.episode_object: the Denisova 3 finger bone in the comparative record
tuples.time_place_scope: layer 11 of the East Chamber at Denisova Cave, Altai Mountains, about 50 ka
tuples.mechanism: a single Siberian bone yielded the genome that defines the population it belongs to
tuples.evidence_lens: the Siberian genome used as the reference against which the Gansu proteins were read

tuples.episode_object: the sediment DNA profiles from the Siberian cave
tuples.time_place_scope: the Main Chamber deposits of Denisova Cave, Altai, about 100 ka
tuples.mechanism: sediment layers in a second cave record the same population across a long occupation
tuples.evidence_lens: the two sediment records compared to map the population's geographic range

tuples.episode_object: the Harbin cranium held in northeastern China
tuples.time_place_scope: the river gravels near Harbin, Heilongjiang, at least 146 ka
tuples.mechanism: a large archaic skull was recovered from bridge works and kept out of sight for decades
tuples.evidence_lens: protein and shape evidence weighed in placing that skull beside the Gansu material

tuples.episode_object: the Penghu 1 jaw dredged from the seabed
tuples.time_place_scope: the Penghu channel off western Taiwan, middle Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: a robust jaw was dredged from a drowned land surface exposed at lower sea levels
tuples.evidence_lens: protein sequencing of that jaw compared with the Gansu peptide results

tuples.episode_object: the high-altitude tool assemblage from central Tibet
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nwya Devu site on the Tibetan Plateau, Tibet, about 40 ka
tuples.mechanism: blade production at 4,600 metres shows sustained occupation of the high plateau
tuples.evidence_lens: the altitude record read alongside the modern Tibetan high-altitude gene variant

tuples.episode_object: the monastery record of the specimen's keeping
tuples.time_place_scope: the temple beside the cave in the Ganjia Basin, Gansu, since 1980
tuples.mechanism: a find handed to a religious institution stayed in one place until it was studied
tuples.evidence_lens: the chain of custody reconstructed from monastery accounts and university records

tuples.episode_object: the Sungir 1 skeleton with rows of beads along the garment line
tuples.time_place_scope: grave 1 on the Klyazma River terrace near Vladimir, MIS 3
tuples.mechanism: beads sewn to clothing keep their rows when a body decays inside a filled grave
tuples.evidence_lens: bead positions mapped to reconstruct the garment they were once stitched onto

tuples.episode_object: the two juveniles laid head to head in a single pit
tuples.time_place_scope: the double grave beneath the occupation layer at Sungir, MIS 3
tuples.mechanism: a single pit dug and filled in one episode holds bodies in a fixed arrangement
tuples.evidence_lens: grave fill and the layer above compared to confirm both were interred together

tuples.episode_object: flint blades and points collected from the living floor
tuples.time_place_scope: the cultural layer above the graves at Sungir, the last glacial
tuples.mechanism: blade blanks were struck from prepared cores and shaped into points and burins
tuples.evidence_lens: the assemblage placed between the Streletskian and eastern Gravettian traditions

tuples.episode_object: a human femoral shaft packed tight with red pigment
tuples.time_place_scope: the ochre lens beneath the bodies in the double grave at Sungir
tuples.mechanism: a shaft cleaned of its ends can be filled with powdered pigment and set upright
tuples.evidence_lens: the pigment analysed and the shaft's sex and age assessed from its own bone

tuples.episode_object: a loess column sampled for grain size and magnetic properties
tuples.time_place_scope: the loess cover over the Sungir deposits, Vladimir region, the last glacial
tuples.mechanism: windblown silt accumulated across the plain and buried the terrace surface
tuples.evidence_lens: luminescence ages on the silt read together with the radiocarbon series on bone

tuples.episode_object: the field drawings made during the first exploratory season
tuples.time_place_scope: the 1957 trench cut into the Sungir terrace, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: a clay pit exposure led to trenching that first revealed the buried living floor
tuples.evidence_lens: the early drawings compared with later plans to fix the position of each find

tuples.episode_object: straightened mammoth ivory lances lifted beside the children
tuples.time_place_scope: the 1969 excavation area at Sungir, Vladimir region, MIS 3
tuples.mechanism: ivory softened and straightened can be worked into a long, rigid shaft
tuples.evidence_lens: the working traces read against experimental attempts to straighten tusk ivory

tuples.episode_object: ash and burnt bone lifted from a fireplace on the floor
tuples.time_place_scope: the hearth cluster in the Sungir occupation layer, the last glacial
tuples.mechanism: bone burnt as fuel leaves calcined fragments concentrated around a fireplace
tuples.evidence_lens: hearth contents compared with the fauna to show which species were burnt

tuples.episode_object: a measured section drawn through the river terrace deposits
tuples.time_place_scope: the Klyazma River terrace section near Vladimir, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: river terraces build and are then draped by silt as a valley continues to cut down
tuples.evidence_lens: the section tied to the depth at which each grave was cut into the terrace

tuples.episode_object: trays of ivory beads and a belt of arctic fox canines
tuples.time_place_scope: the Moscow museum collection holding the Sungir finds, late Pleistocene material
tuples.mechanism: ivory blanks were cut, drilled and rounded in a repeated sequence of steps
tuples.evidence_lens: bead counts and drilling traces used to estimate the labour each garment took

tuples.episode_object: the Markina Gora skeleton and the genome sequenced from it
tuples.time_place_scope: Kostenki 14 at Markina Gora, Don Valley, Russia, about 37 ka
tuples.mechanism: a crouched body placed in an ochre-lined pit keeps its posture as the pit fills
tuples.evidence_lens: the Don Valley genome compared with the Sungir individuals in one population study

tuples.episode_object: ivory and bone tools curated from a Don Valley settlement
tuples.time_place_scope: Kostenki 12 on the Don, Voronezh region, about 40 ka
tuples.mechanism: settlement floors accumulate tools and debris around dwellings and storage pits
tuples.evidence_lens: the Kostenki sequence used as the framework for placing the Sungir occupation

tuples.episode_object: the ochre-covered skulls of a triple grave in Moravia
tuples.time_place_scope: the Dolni Vestonice triple burial, Moravia, about 31 ka
tuples.mechanism: pigment placed on the head and pelvis leaves stained bone where it lay thickest
tuples.evidence_lens: staining patterns compared between the Moravian and Russian graves

tuples.episode_object: ivory ornaments recorded across a Moravian living floor
tuples.time_place_scope: Pavlov I, southern Moravia, about 30 ka
tuples.mechanism: ornament production on a settlement leaves blanks, failures and finished pieces together
tuples.evidence_lens: production stages at Pavlov used to interpret the finished beads from Sungir

tuples.episode_object: the Brno 2 male burial with its jointed ivory figurine
tuples.time_place_scope: the Brno 2 grave, Moravia, about 30 ka
tuples.mechanism: grave goods of ivory and shell were placed with a body under a covering of ochre
tuples.evidence_lens: the Moravian grave goods listed beside the Sungir assemblage in one inventory

tuples.episode_object: the remains of a Siberian child and the library built from them
tuples.time_place_scope: Mal'ta on the Belaya River, southern Siberia, about 24 ka
tuples.mechanism: cold burial conditions preserve nuclear DNA in the dense bone of the skull base
tuples.evidence_lens: the Siberian genome and the Sungir genomes placed on the same ancestry tree

tuples.episode_object: ivory foreshafts and beads from an Arctic river bank site
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yana Rhinoceros Horn Site, Arctic Siberia, about 32 ka
tuples.mechanism: permafrost holds worked ivory and bone in a state close to how it was discarded
tuples.evidence_lens: the Yana ornament forms compared with the Russian plain assemblages of that age

tuples.episode_object: an infant grave covered with a dense spread of beads
tuples.time_place_scope: Krems-Wachtberg, Lower Austria, about 31 ka
tuples.mechanism: infants placed under a shoulder blade and beads were buried within a settlement area
tuples.evidence_lens: the Austrian infant graves read alongside the juvenile treatment seen at Sungir

tuples.episode_object: the ornamented burial known to excavators as the Prince
tuples.time_place_scope: Arene Candide, Liguria, Italy, about 28 ka
tuples.mechanism: shell ornaments and a flint blade were arranged on a body laid in an ochre bed
tuples.evidence_lens: the Ligurian and Russian graves compared for the labour their ornaments required

tuples.episode_object: shell and bone ornaments recorded in a Grimaldi cave grave
tuples.time_place_scope: the Grotte des Enfants at Grimaldi, Liguria, late Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: coastal groups gathered marine shells and pierced them for stringing as ornaments
tuples.evidence_lens: shell species identified to show how far the ornament materials had travelled

coverage_profiles.subject: the Piltdown forgery and its exposure

tuples.episode_object: the cranial fragments catalogued at the Natural History Museum
tuples.time_place_scope: the Barkham Manor gravel pit at Piltdown, Sussex, dug from 1912
tuples.mechanism: a medieval human braincase was broken up and salted into a gravel pit as a fossil find
tuples.evidence_lens: low fluorine content measured against genuinely ancient bone from those gravels

tuples.episode_object: the ape mandible presented alongside the skull
tuples.time_place_scope: the gravel spread on a terrace above the Sussex Ouse at Piltdown
tuples.mechanism: an orangutan jaw was broken at the joints so it could not be articulated with the skull
tuples.evidence_lens: those breakage points identified as deliberate in the 1953 reinvestigation

tuples.episode_object: the two molars seated in the ape jaw
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sussex pit specimens displayed in London from 1913 onward
tuples.mechanism: the molar cusps were filed flat to imitate the wear pattern of a human chewing surface
tuples.evidence_lens: file marks seen under a microscope and reported in the 1953 Bulletin paper

tuples.episode_object: the isolated canine tooth reported in 1913
tuples.time_place_scope: the Barkham Manor spoil heaps searched during the second field season
tuples.mechanism: the crown was abraded artificially and painted to imitate a worn and stained fossil
tuples.evidence_lens: the paint layer identified chemically and the abrasion separated from natural wear

tuples.episode_object: the carved bone implement known as the cricket bat
tuples.time_place_scope: the Piltdown gravels, from which the implement was reported in 1914
tuples.mechanism: a fossil elephant limb bone was cut with a steel blade into a flat bladed shape
tuples.evidence_lens: cut facets matched to a metal blade rather than to any stone tool edge

tuples.episode_object: the Stegodon molar recorded from the pit
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sussex gravel pit finds attributed to a Pleistocene river terrace
tuples.mechanism: a fossil tooth from a North African deposit was introduced into an English gravel pit
tuples.evidence_lens: uranium content matched to Tunisian fossils rather than to Sussex gravels

tuples.episode_object: the hippopotamus tooth from the same gravel
tuples.time_place_scope: the assemblage of exotic fossils reported from the Piltdown site
tuples.mechanism: a tooth from a Mediterranean island deposit was added to the supposed local fauna
tuples.evidence_lens: its radiometric signature compared with Maltese cave fossils held in London

tuples.episode_object: the second set of finds attributed to Sheffield Park
tuples.time_place_scope: the field some miles from Barkham Manor, reported as a second locality
tuples.mechanism: a matching skull fragment and molar were placed elsewhere to confirm the first finds
tuples.evidence_lens: the second site material tested by the same fluorine method as the originals

tuples.episode_object: Arthur Smith Woodward's 1913 reconstruction of the skull
tuples.time_place_scope: the Geological Society of London proceedings for the 1912 announcement
tuples.mechanism: the fragments were assembled into one individual with a large brain and an ape jaw
tuples.evidence_lens: the reconstruction disputed at the time by Arthur Keith using those same fragments

tuples.episode_object: the John Cooke painting of the assembled committee
tuples.time_place_scope: the London scientific circles examining the finds between 1912 and 1915
tuples.mechanism: the canvas recorded the group of men who authenticated the assembled specimens
tuples.evidence_lens: the sitters' published statements read against later analytical results on the fossils

tuples.episode_object: Kenneth Oakley's fluorine test result sheets
tuples.time_place_scope: the British Museum laboratories, where testing began in 1949
tuples.mechanism: buried bone takes up fluorine from groundwater in proportion to the time it lay there
tuples.evidence_lens: skull and jaw values compared with genuinely old bone from the same gravel body

tuples.episode_object: the nitrogen measurements made on the bone samples
tuples.time_place_scope: the analytical programme on the Piltdown material during the early 1950s
tuples.mechanism: collagen nitrogen falls steadily in buried bone as the protein breaks down over time
tuples.evidence_lens: nitrogen readings set beside fluorine values as two independent age indicators

tuples.episode_object: the stained outer surface of a cranial fragment
tuples.time_place_scope: the specimens as they appeared when first shown at Piltdown, Sussex
tuples.mechanism: the bones were stained with an iron and chromium solution to match the gravel colour
tuples.evidence_lens: chromium detected chemically, a metal absent from the gravel the finds came from

tuples.episode_object: the gravel section drawn at the discovery pit
tuples.time_place_scope: the terrace gravel of the Sussex Ouse valley, mapped as Pleistocene
tuples.mechanism: a shallow pit dug for road metal exposed the gravel the finds were said to lie in
tuples.evidence_lens: the pit's stratigraphy re-examined against regional terrace mapping of the valley

tuples.episode_object: the flint implements reported alongside the skull
tuples.time_place_scope: the artefact finds from the Barkham Manor pit between 1912 and 1915
tuples.mechanism: flints were stained to the colour of the gravel before being placed in the deposit
tuples.evidence_lens: staining chemistry on the flints compared with that on the bone specimens

tuples.episode_object: the plaster casts distributed to museums worldwide
tuples.time_place_scope: the international circulation of the Piltdown material from 1913 onward
tuples.mechanism: casts spread the reconstruction to institutions that never examined the originals
tuples.evidence_lens: casts compared with the originals once the specimens were reopened for testing

tuples.episode_object: the type description naming Eoanthropus dawsoni
tuples.time_place_scope: the 1913 publication of the Sussex finds in a London journal
tuples.mechanism: a new genus and species were erected on a composite of human and ape material
tuples.evidence_lens: the name formally set aside once that composite nature had been demonstrated

tuples.episode_object: the orangutan jaw source traced by DNA sequencing
tuples.time_place_scope: the museum specimens re-examined in a 2016 analytical study
tuples.mechanism: a single ape jaw supplied the mandible and the isolated teeth attributed to the site
tuples.evidence_lens: mitochondrial sequences and computed tomography scans read as one combined result

tuples.episode_object: the dental putty packed into the tooth sockets
tuples.time_place_scope: the interior cavities of the Piltdown specimens revealed by scanning
tuples.mechanism: gravel and putty were packed into hollows to weight the pieces and hold them together
tuples.evidence_lens: the packing revealed by microtomography of the sealed interior spaces

tuples.episode_object: Charles Dawson's correspondence held in the museum archive
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sussex antiquarian circles active before the 1912 announcement
tuples.mechanism: letters record the order in which each find was reported and to whom it was shown
tuples.evidence_lens: the letters read alongside the record of earlier fakes traced to that collector
